newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- firm tone, list appears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- firm tone, list appears.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were unchanged but firm early Thursday after outperforming Treasuries on Wednesday.
"The bid-side is very firm, but I don't hear much trading right now," one trader said.

The trader said a modest bid-wanted list had begun circulating and would probably set the tone for early action. He said included on the list were Chicago water bonds and Port Authority of New York and New Jersey debt.

The Labor Department said U.S. initial state jobless benefit claims rose to 337,000 the week ended May 31, up from a revised 318,000 the prior week. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a figure of 320,000.
After the data, the government long bond was up 1/32 at 96-25/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
April housing completions are set for release at 1000 EDT, but the real waiting game is for Friday's May jobs report. Economists polled by Reuters expect a 219,000 increase in non-farm payrolls.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was unchanged at 116-2/32, while September T-bonds were off 1/32 at 110. The MOB spread widened to 194 ticks from 193 at the close on Wednesday.

In secondary trading, bids on Alliance Airport Authority, Texas, 6-3/8s of 2021 were unchanged at 101-1/2. New York State Energy Research and Development Authority MBIA 5-1/2s of 2021 were up one basis point to 5.69 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday are expected to total $113 million in 17 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings are expected to total $33 million in two sales, with a $21 million South Carolina Housing Finance Development Authority deal through Goldmann, Sachs & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $80 million are scheduled. A $18 million Cupertino Unified School District, Calif., deal is the largest.
